title: Relative higher direct image continuity with varying base
statement:
Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset and let $u_i:V_i\to B_i$ be an inverse system of scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme], with affine transition maps [pqf-def-affine-morphism] $a_{ji}:V_j\to V_i$ and $b_{ji}:B_j\to B_i$ for $j\geq i$, satisfying $u_i a_{ji}=b_{ji}u_j$. Suppose every $u_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The transition maps satisfy $a_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $b_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $a_{ki}=a_{ji}a_{kj}$ and $b_{ki}=b_{ji}b_{kj}$ for $k\geq j\geq i$. Let $u:V\to B$ be the inverse limit (the compatible projection cones of $V$ and $B$ are universal among such cones), and write $a_i:V\to V_i$ and $b_i:B\to B_i$ for its projections. Let $A_i$ be abelian sheaves on the small etale sites of $V_i$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with transition morphisms $\phi_{ji}:a_{ji}^{-1}A_i\to A_j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws under the canonical inverse-image composition identifications [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Put $A=\varinjlim_i a_i^{-1}A_i$, a colimit in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every integer $q\geq0$, the canonical morphism of abelian sheaves on $B_{\Et}$ is an isomorphism:
$$
 C_u:\varinjlim_i b_i^{-1}R^q u_{i,*}A_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R^q u_*A.
$$
Here $R^q u_*$ is the higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The transition morphism from index $i$ to $j$ is obtained by pulling back to $B$ the degree-$q$ exchange for the commutative square $(a_{ji},b_{ji},u_j,u_i)$, then applying $R^q u_{j,*}$ to $\phi_{ji}$. The leg to $R^q u_*A$ is the same construction with $(a_i,b_i,u,u_i)$ and the coprojection $a_i^{-1}A_i\to A$. Exchange here means the mate of the canonical inverse-image square isomorphism [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange]; the construction uses only commutativity of the square and does not require it to be cartesian. These specified transitions and legs define the displayed comparison. No torsion hypothesis and no cartesianness of the transition squares are required.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, statement and construction of the comparison in the first two paragraphs of its proof

proof.text: Use the commutative-square exchange of [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange], whose inverse-image square isomorphism is constructed from composition and the commutativity equality, with no cartesian hypothesis. Write $G_i=R^qu_{i,*}A_i$ and let $\psi_{ji}:b_{ji}^{-1}G_i\to G_j$ be exchange followed by $R^qu_{j,*}(\phi_{ji})$, as specified in the statement. These maps satisfy the system and cone laws. Indeed the square isomorphism for $k\to i$ is the pasted square isomorphism for $k\to j\to i$: both are the composition comparison between inverse images along the equal maps $u_i a_{ki}=b_{ki}u_k$, by associativity of the inverse-image composition isomorphisms. Apply part (1) of mate pasting to these isomorphisms and part (4) to the identity square. Naturality in the coefficient, followed by $\phi_{ki}=\phi_{kj}\circ a_{kj}^{-1}\phi_{ji}$, gives $\psi_{ki}=\psi_{kj}\circ b_{kj}^{-1}\psi_{ji}$, with the composition identifications understood. For the cone law write $c_i:a_i^{-1}A_i\to A$ for the coprojections, $E_i:b_i^{-1}G_i\to R^qu_*a_i^{-1}A_i$ for projection exchange, and $\lambda_i=R^qu_*(c_i)\circ E_i$. Pasting the transition square $j\to i$ with the projection square at $j$ gives projection exchange at $i$. Naturality of its mate in $A_i$ therefore rewrites $\lambda_j\circ b_j^{-1}\psi_{ji}$ as $R^qu_*(c_j\circ a_j^{-1}\phi_{ji})\circ E_i$. The colimit cocone relation $c_j\circ a_j^{-1}\phi_{ji}=c_i$ makes this $\lambda_i$, under the inverse-image composition identifications. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology respects these equalities because inverse image is exact. Thus $L=\varinjlim_i b_i^{-1}G_i$ and the specified map $C_u:L\to R^qu_*A$ are defined. This is an application of abstract mates to commutative squares, so no cartesian-square exchange-pasting statement is being used.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, first two proof paragraphs, construction and compatibility of the comparison

proof.text: Fix $i_0$ and restrict to the tail $j\ge i_0$. This does not change the inverse limits: a cone over the tail extends to index $i$ by choosing $j\ge i,i_0$ and composing its leg with the transition to $i$; two choices agree after passing to a common upper bound. The same argument extends cocones of the pulled-back coefficient and higher-image diagrams, so their colimits and comparison are unchanged. The identity and composition laws established in step 1 ensure these extensions respect all arrows.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof: localization on inverse-image affine opens

proof.text: Cover $B_{i_0}$ by affine opens $W_{i_0}$ and put $W_j=b_{ji_0}^{-1}W_{i_0}$, $Z_j=u_j^{-1}W_j$. Affine-morphism permanence makes $W_j$ affine. The qcqs base-change and source-permanence clauses make $Z_j\to W_j$ qcqs and $Z_j$ qcqs. Commutativity gives $Z_j=a_{ji_0}^{-1}(u_{i_0}^{-1}W_{i_0})$. Apply open restriction of affine-transition limits separately to the $B_j$ and $V_j$: their restricted limits are $W=b_{i_0}^{-1}W_{i_0}$ and $Z=u^{-1}W$. That same lemma supplies affine restricted transitions. These $W$ cover $B$.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof: localization on inverse-image affine opens

proof.text: Apply the tail-open coefficient lemma to the source system with $g_0=u_{i_0}:V_{i_0}\to B_{i_0}$ and the open $W_{i_0}$. It gives the coherent restricted $A_j|_{Z_j}$ system, its colimit $A|_Z$, and the restricted coefficient legs. Apply it also to the base system with sheaves $G_j$ and $g_0=\mathrm{id}_{B_{i_0}}$; it identifies $L|_W$ with the colimit of the pulled-back $G_j|_{W_j}$, with the specified restricted transitions. Open inverse image is restriction by the etale restriction lemma.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof: localization on inverse-image affine opens

proof.text: Open inclusions are etale, so etale-localization exchange and exact-inverse-image cohomology give $G_j|_{W_j}\cong R^q(u_j|_{Z_j})_*(A_j|_{Z_j})$ and $(R^qu_*A)|_W\cong R^q(u|_Z)_*(A|_Z)$. For any transition or projection square write its arrows as $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$. Let $W\subseteq Y$, $W'=g^{-1}W$, $Z=f^{-1}W$, $Z'=f'^{-1}W'$, with open inclusions $j,j',k,k'$. Apply the exchange-cube lemma with $(X_0,Y_0,S_0,T_0)=(Y',X',Y,X)$, $(X_1,Y_1,S_1,T_1)=(W',Z',W,Z)$ and $(x,y,s,a)=(j',k',j,k)$. Its $E_0,E_1$ are original and restricted exchange; its $P,Q$ are the localization exchanges for $f,f'$. Indeed the faces $(f,f|_Z,j,k)$ and $(f',f'|_{Z'},j',k')$ are cartesian, since $Z=f^{-1}W=X\times_YW$ and $Z'=X'\times_{Y'}W'$. The cartesian-square exchange of the localization lemma is the mate of the derived square isomorphism, in which only the equality of composites enters. That isomorphism is the class of the termwise sheaf-level composite $c^{-1}\circ c$ along that equality. By clause (2) of derived inverse-image composition, this is the commutative-square isomorphism $\theta$. So the two exchange definitions give the same morphisms $P,Q$, and these are isomorphisms. All six faces commute by restriction and the original square equality. The cube equation, taking degree $q$ through exact inverse images, identifies original exchange restricted to $W'$ with restricted-square exchange under these localization isomorphisms and inverse-image composition comparisons. Coefficient naturality and the restricted legs in step 4 identify the coefficient maps too. Thus $C_u|_W$ is exactly the canonical comparison for $Z_j\to W_j$.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof: localization on inverse-image affine opens

proof.text: It remains to prove the restricted comparisons are isomorphisms on every $W$. Indeed local injectivity and local surjectivity on these opens give the same two properties on $B$, and the locally-bijective sheafification criterion then gives the original isomorphism. By steps 3--5 each restricted problem has affine bases, qcqs sources, affine transitions, the stated limit coefficients, and exactly the specified comparison. Rename this restricted system $V_j\to B_j$ for the rest of the proof.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof: localization on inverse-image affine opens

proof.text:
Use the equivalence between abelian sheaves on the small etale site and the finite-cover affine etale site. By the affine-etale colimit theorem, every affine etale $U\to B$ has a model $U_i\to B_i$, and all its base changes $U_j=U_i\times_{B_i}B_j$ for $j\ge i$ are affine. The theorem also supplies strictification, descent of morphisms and descent of finite standard covers. Apply cohomology of colimit sites in degree zero to the system $G_j$ with transitions $\psi_{kj}$. Since $H^0(U_j,G_j)=G_j(U_j)$, this gives, canonically and with the specified transition maps,
$$L(U)=\varinjlim_{j\ge i}G_j(U_j).$$
Here the restriction equivalences identify the inverse images and their units: their right adjoints on each affine test object are the same evaluation on its base change, so uniqueness of the left adjoint gives the unit-compatible identifications. Site equivalences preserve the colimit by its universal property. The degree-zero specialization is used only for sections of $G_j$, not for the higher direct images themselves.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof, first displayed equality, using Sites Tag 09YN

proof.text:
For this model set $T_j=V_j\times_{B_j}U_j$ and $T=V\times_BU$. Each $T_j$ is qcqs: $T_j\to U_j$ is a base change of the qcqs $u_j$, and $U_j$ is affine. For $k\ge j$, $T_k\cong V_k\times_{V_j}T_j$, because $U_k=U_j\times_{B_j}B_k$ and the original square commutes. Thus $T_k\to T_j$ is affine, even though $V_k\to V_j$ need not be a base change of $B_k\to B_j$. The projections exhibit $T=\varprojlim_{j\ge i}T_j$: maps to the $T_j$ amount to compatible maps to the $V_j$ and $U_j$ with equal images in the $B_j$, hence to maps to $V$ and $U$ with equal images in $B$. Restrict $A_j$ to $T_j$ and call it $A_{j,T_j}$. The induced coefficient system has limit coefficient $A|_T$, since inverse images compose and commute with colimits. The cohomology-continuity theorem for varying abelian sheaves consequently gives the canonical isomorphism
$$\alpha_U:\varinjlim_{j\ge i}H^q(T_j,A_{j,T_j})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T,A|_T).$$
The maps are exactly pullback on cohomology followed by the coefficient transitions. This argument applies after any replacement of $U_i$ by an affine etale object at any later stage.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof, left vertical arrow in the cohomology/sheaf diagram

proof.text:
Put $P_j(U_j)=H^q(T_j,A_{j,T_j})$ and $P(U)=H^q(T,A|_T)$, with canonical sheafification maps $\theta_j:P_j(U_j)\to G_j(U_j)$ and $\theta:P(U)\to(R^qu_*A)(U)$. The commutative-square chart compatibility lemma, first for a transition square and then for a projection square, followed by naturality for the coefficient maps, gives
$$C_u(U)\circ h_U=\theta\circ\alpha_U,$$
where $h_U:\varinjlim_{j\ge i}P_j(U_j)\to L(U)$ is induced by the $\theta_j$ and the section formula of step 7. In particular, this is a commutative diagram with top row $\varinjlim P_j\to L(U)$, bottom row $P(U)\to R^qu_*A(U)$, left vertical arrow $\alpha_U$ an isomorphism, and right vertical arrow the specified $C_u(U)$. It is a diagram for the actual mate-defined comparison, not just for some isomorphism between the objects.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof, commutative cohomology/sheaf diagram

proof.text: Let $s\in(R^qu_*A)(U)$. Locally on $U$, the sheafification description and local representation provide $z\in P(U)$ mapping to $s$; refine the cover by affine etale objects. Each such object has a model at some stage by affine-etale descent, and step 8 gives $z=\alpha_U(\zeta)$ for a class $\zeta\in\varinjlim_jP_j(U_j)$. Then step 9 gives $C_u(h_U(\zeta))=s$. Thus $C_u$ is locally surjective on the affine etale site.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof, local surjectivity (1)

proof.text: Let $\xi\in L(U)$ have $C_u(\xi)=0$. By the section formula of step 7 and the elementwise description of a filtered colimit of abelian groups (integer modules), choose a stage $j\ge i$ and $\xi_j\in G_j(U_j)$ representing $\xi$. Since $G_j$ is the sheafification of $P_j$, there is a finite standard affine etale cover $\{U_{j,k}\to U_j\}$ on which $\xi_j$ lifts to $z_{j,k}\in H^q(V_j\times_{B_j}U_{j,k},A_j)$. Pull this cover back to $U$ and work on one member. Step 9 says the image of the pulled-back raw class in $R^qu_*A$ is zero. The local-equality property of sheafification, applied to that raw class and zero, gives a further affine etale cover on which the raw limit class itself is zero. Descend each of these affine objects to some stage. Choose a common upper bound of that stage and $j$, then use morphism descent to represent its map to $U_{j,k}$ after enlarging this upper bound once more. The coefficient on the new chart is pulled back from $A_j$ and mapped into the later $A_l$ by the given coefficient transition; this is exactly the restriction of the original raw class in the system of step 8, by the coefficient and test-object naturality in step 9. Different covering members may use different later stages, since we seek local vanishing. On each resulting object step 8 applies, so injectivity of $\alpha$ says that the restricted raw class is zero in the colimit of the $P_l$. Its image under $h$ is therefore zero. That image is precisely the restriction of $\xi$, by the diagram of step 9 and the restriction maps of the stage sheafification maps. Hence $\xi$ is locally zero. This does not infer global vanishing of a cohomology class from vanishing of its sheafification; the second local refinement is essential.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, second proof, local injectivity (2), including the second local replacement

proof.text: For any two local sections with equal images, apply step 11 to their difference. Thus $C_u$ is locally injective as well as locally surjective. Apply the locally-bijective criterion for sheafification to this morphism viewed as a map of presheaves of abelian groups; its source and target are already sheaves, so their sheafifications are themselves. It follows that $C_u$ is an isomorphism on the affine etale site, hence on the small etale site by the restriction equivalence. Finally the open cover in step 6 gives local injectivity and local surjectivity on the original base, and the same criterion gives the original isomorphism. All cohomology-continuity and sheafification results used here apply to arbitrary abelian sheaves, including nontorsion ones.
